subject: Small language problems (sum of integers; multi_normal with covariance matrix created on the fly)

messages.author: 074998f49d84156c
messages.subject: Small language problems (sum of integers; multi_normal with covariance matrix created on the fly)
parts:
Hello,

I was playing around with Poisson and Multinomial distributions. I tried to use the function 'sum' on an array of integers to assign the total on another integer variable, but this function only returns reals. I thought of declaring the total as real, but then I couldn't assign it a Poisson distribution in the model part of the program, since poisson_log only works with int.

In the end I summed manually with a loop:

  int<lower=0> y[N, K];
  int<lower=0> y_total[N];

  for (n in 1:N) {
    y_total[n] <- 0;
    for (k in 1:K)
      y_total[n] <- y_total[n] + y[n, k];
  }


It would be useful to have 'sum' defined for integers and be able to simply do:

  int<lower=0> y[N, K];
  int<lower=0> y_total[N];

  for (n in 1:N)
    y_total[n] <- sum(y[n]);



Another language concern I encountered is that when I tried

    y ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0, 5), diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, 5)));

stan failed to compile with a lengthy error message (file attached). If I first assign diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, 5))to a variable and use it in the sampling statement, then it works.


Also, as it is my first message on the list I would like to thank everyone involved in the Stan project!

Kind regards,
Lionel Henry

> y_total[n] <- sum(y[n]);

Makes sense. We can add a sum() for integers.

We've tried to clearly distinguish integer from real, and
have been implementing functions with various types as quickly
as we can.

> Another language concern I encountered is that when I tried
>
> y ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0, 5), diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, 5)));
>
> stan failed to compile with a lengthy error message (file attached). If I first assign diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, 5))to a
> variable and use it in the sampling statement, then it works.

Thanks for forwarding --- they don't call them "error novels" for nothing :-)
This is definitely a bug --- we don't want code to get translated to
C++ by stanc that then fails to compile.

This looks at first glance like another problem with int types.
Could you please send the list (or just me) the model you were
trying to compile? If not, I will try and guess what type you
have for y.

Two points on how Stan models work:

1. unless y is a parameter, that sampling statement has no effect, and

2. in this particular case, it's more efficient using the
vectorized non-multivariate:

y ~ normal(0,1);

which will do the same thing because the mean vector is
constant and the covariance matrix is diagonal.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Small language problems (sum of integers; multi_normal with covariance matrix created on the fly)
parts:
The good news is that it's already fixed for 2.0 :-)

I could replicate the bug with Stan 1.3 and this
model:

parameters {
vector[5] y;
}
model {
y ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0,5),
diag_matrix(rep_vector(0,5)));
}

It crashes and burns in the C++ compiler in Stan 1.3, but
compiles just fine in current 2.0 development branch.

The workaround in 1.3 is to explicitly use double literals,

parameters {
vector[5] y;
}
model {
y ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0.0,5),
diag_matrix(rep_vector(0.0,5)));
}

[Note the 0.0 instead of 0.]

What Stan 1.3 was trying to do was create a vector of integers,
which can't be assigned to a vector of double in Eigen, our matrix
lib.

Thanks again for reporting the issue --- we really appreciate
it.

- Bob

P.S. I added an integer sum() to our to-do list.
